Status colours, side by side

Today's palette and three candidates, shot on the same four map views (the app's Map tab, today's statuses, Expo web at a 390 × 844 phone viewport). Pick a view, a ground and a colour-vision simulation; the numbers under each map are the worst ΔE2000 for that theme across normal vision and protan, deutan and tritan simulation (Viénot 1999 and Machado 2009). Twenty is a different category at a glance on a thin line; under twelve, two lines read as one. Tap a map for the full-size shot.

Numbers: line = both colours as thin lines over the same ground (coverage 0.6, boundaries 0.8), worst ground; lake = both as lake fills over the basemap's water; sat = thin lines over the satellite grounds. boundary = the worst of the region and unit boundary against all five statuses (closed, own, base, restricted, open). The colour-blind palette and satellite rows use their own theme's colours (satellite draws the light theme). Source: T47-colours.md, scripts/measure.mjs. In A, B and C the unit boundary wears the region's colour on purpose and is told apart by width and dash.
